issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'עֵבֶר הַנָּהָר' means 'beyond the River' (i.e., the region beyond the Euphrates), but the Chinese renders it as '以巴衛的大河' (the great river of Ibawi), treating 'עֵבֶר' as a proper name '以巴衛' rather than the common noun 'beyond/side'. This changes the geographical meaning: the Hebrew says he ruled over all the region beyond the River (Euphrates), from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River; the Chinese instead says he ruled 'the great river of Ibawi' and 'all kings of Ibawi', which is a substantive mistranslation of a key term.
